question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the following sentence.

Independence Day is considered as a __red-letter day__ in the history of India.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"red-letter day"** means a day that is pleasantly noteworthy or memorable. (स्मरणीय दिन)

 
 
• **Example: **Graduation day is a** red-letter day** in every student's life.
 
 
 
• **"Memorable day"** refers to a day that is worth remembering because it is special or significant. (यादगार दिन)
 
 
• **Example: **The day I got my first job is a **memorable day** for me.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Memorable day.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Uneventful day** (अघटनापूर्ण दिन): A day when nothing significant or exciting happens.

 
 
• **Example:** Yesterday was quite an** uneventful day**; I just stayed home and watched TV.
 
 
 
• **Unimportant day** (महत्वहीन दिन): A day that does not have any significant importance or relevance.
 
 
• **Example:** It was just another **unimportant day** in my routine.
 
 
 
• **Regular day** (साधारण दिन): A day that is typical or routine with no special events.
 
 
• **Example:** It was a** regular day** at the office with the usual tasks and meetings.
